items.label: Carbon dioxide
items.quote: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and can be trapped in low areas in concentrations that are deadly

items.label: Fluorine
items.quote: Fluorine, which in high concentrations is toxic, can be adsorbed onto volcanic ash particles that later fall to the ground.

items.label: Sulfur dioxide gas
items.quote: Sulfur dioxide gas can react with water droplets in the atmosphere to create acid rain

items.label: Mudflows
items.quote: Mudflows or debris flows composed mostly of volcanic materials on the flanks of a volcano are called lahars.

items.label: These flows of mud, rock, and water
items.quote: These flows of mud, rock, and water can rush down valleys and stream channels at speeds of 20 to 40 miles per hour and can travel more than 50 miles.

items.label: Some lahars contain so much rock debris
items.quote: Some lahars contain so much rock debris (60 to 90% by weight) that they look like fast-moving rivers of wet concrete.
